t: The siege lasted two months, from 14 July to 12 September 1683, and the relief army and the garrison together defeated the Ottoman army in a single day.
Strengths are disputed: the Ottoman army in the battle is given as 28,400 to 50,000 men, and the relief army as 65,000 or as 70,000–80,000.
The Ottomans fought on until 1699, when the Treaty of Karlowitz ceded much of Hungary to the Habsburgs.
dyk: Before the siege the Ottoman Empire and the Holy Roman Empire had been at peace for 20 years under the Peace of Vasvár, and the allied cavalry charge on 12 September has been called the largest known cavalry charge in history.
ev: Imre Thököly, reinforced by an Ottoman contingent, is recognised by the Ottomans as King of Upper Hungary
The Ottoman army is mobilised on 21 January and war is declared on 6 August
The Treaty of Warsaw binds the Holy Roman Empire and Poland to mutual support
The main Ottoman army reaches Vienna and Kara Mustafa demands its surrender
The Poles under Sobieski cross the Danube at Tulln to join the imperial troops
The Ottomans occupy the Burg ravelin and the low wall nearby
The relief army attacks and defeats the Ottoman army, ending the siege
The Treaty of Karlowitz cedes much of Hungary to the Habsburgs

f.date: 12 September 1683, the last day of a siege that began on 14 July 1683
f.place: Kahlenberg and the ground north-west of Vienna, then the Habsburg capital, in present-day Austria
f.sides: The Holy Roman Empire and the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth under King John III Sobieski, with Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg commanding the garrison; the relief army is put at 65,000 soldiers with 165–200 guns by one assessment, and at 70,000–80,000 by another. The Ottoman Empire under Grand Vizier Kara Mustafa Pasha, with an army given as 28,400 to 50,000 in the battle
f.outcome: The relief army defeated the Ottomans and Vienna was saved. The Ottomans fought on until 1699 and lost control of Hungary and Transylvania.
